Topic at a glance
Public Corporations and Government Undertakings — Control, Autonomy and Accountability is a registered theme in Administrative Law. Public Corporations and Government Undertakings — Control, Autonomy and Accountability is governed by constitutional judicial review, administrative law principles, delegated legislation and Lokpal and Lokayuktas Act, 2013. identify the source of power, statutory duty, decision-maker, affected right, alternative remedy and standard of review applicable to the administrative action.

Provenance, purpose and doctrinal foundation
The topic exists to organise a legally enforceable rule, doctrine or professional procedure. Read the statutory text, constitutional setting, institutional purpose and binding authorities together. The correct analysis begins with the legal question and avoids replacing the governing enactment with a generic textbook summary.

cases.name: Praga Tools Corporation v. C.A. Imanual
cases.facts: The Court considered whether a public-sector corporation was amenable to writ jurisdiction.
cases.issue: When can a public corporation be subjected to public-law remedies?
cases.ratioDecidendi: A writ may issue where a public authority has a public duty; the precise remedy depends on the nature of the duty and statutory/public-law obligation.
cases.holding: The Court explained the limits of writ relief against a company.
cases.relevance: Use for public corporations and public-law accountability.

cases.name: Sukhdev Singh v. Bhagatram Sardar Singh Raghuvanshi
cases.facts: The status of statutory corporations and their employees under Article 12 was considered.
cases.issue: When can statutory corporations be treated as instrumentalities of the State?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Statutory corporations exercising public functions may fall within the constitutional conception of State and are subject to fundamental-rights constraints.
cases.holding: The Court treated the named statutory corporations as State instrumentalities.
cases.relevance: Use for constitutional status of public corporations.

cases.name: Ajay Hasia v. Khalid Mujib Sehravardi
cases.facts: The Court considered whether a society managing a regional engineering college was an instrumentality or agency of government.
cases.issue: What factors determine whether an entity is an instrumentality of the State?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Article 12 turns on the substance of governmental control and functional character rather than corporate form alone.
cases.holding: The Court articulated indicia for determining State agency.
cases.relevance: Use for public corporations and government-controlled entities.
